budgetBasis: Illustrative planning allowances per person for 4 days and 3 nights, with 2 adults sharing a room. Excludes flights, shopping, insurance and Tripanize Premium. These are not live quotes.
scheduleBasis: Suggested sightseeing times, not opening hours or confirmed reservations. Reorder days for closures, weather and arrival or departure times. Add an arrival night if you need four full sightseeing days.

guides.title: Bangkok in 4 days
guides.subtitle: Golden temples. Riverside pauses. One more bite.
guides.intro: A first visit built around the river, the old city and Bangkok's food neighbourhoods. Start early, leave room for the heat, and give each part of the city its own time.
guides.base: Choose a hotel near a BTS or MRT station. Silom, Asok and the riverside offer different starting points; check the walk from the actual hotel to the station.
guides.transport: Use the MRT and BTS between districts, river boats for riverside stops, and a taxi when the last stretch is inconvenient. Leave generous transfer time rather than crossing town repeatedly.
guides.packing: Comfortable walking shoes, a refillable bottle, sun protection and a compact rain layer. Carry clothing that meets the Grand Palace and temple dress rules.

days.title: The royal city & the river
days.pace: Temples first, a slower afternoon
days.note: Check the palace's official calendar and dress rules before visiting. Leave the hottest part of the day for lunch and a break.

stops.title: Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew
stops.detail: Give the palace courtyards and temple your full morning rather than squeezing them between other stops.

stops.title: Wat Pho
stops.detail: Continue to the nearby temple complex and its reclining Buddha. Keep shoulders and knees covered.

stops.title: Lunch & a pause around Tha Tien
stops.detail: Choose a sit-down meal and cool off before crossing the river.

stops.title: Wat Arun
stops.detail: Cross to the Thonburi bank and take time with the temple's ceramic details and river views.

stops.title: A riverside dinner
stops.detail: Keep the evening close to the river. Reserve a terrace if a particular view matters to you.

days.food: Around Tha Tien, choose a Thai curry with rice or a simple vegetable stir-fry. For dinner, stay by the river instead of adding another long transfer.
days.planB: If the palace closes for a ceremony, keep Wat Pho and the river, then move the palace to another morning. In heavy rain, postpone the crossing.

days.title: Old trading streets & Chinatown
days.pace: A neighbourhood day with a food-focused finish
days.note: Treat this as a walking route with frequent café stops. Street-food stalls and small businesses keep their own hours.

stops.title: Talat Noi lanes
stops.detail: Look for small shrines, workshop streets and glimpses of the river. Keep clear of working doorways.

stops.title: Lunch near Charoen Krung
stops.detail: Take a proper lunch break, then explore the surrounding shopfronts at your own pace.

stops.title: River City & a café break
stops.detail: Browse whatever exhibitions are on, or use the afternoon for a shaded pause by the river.

stops.title: Chinatown before dinner
stops.detail: Explore the streets around Yaowarat before choosing what to eat. Order a little at a time.

stops.title: A Yaowarat food evening
stops.detail: Make dinner a few small dishes rather than one large meal, with time to sit between stops.

days.food: Try a noodle soup or rice dish for lunch, then choose cooked-to-order dishes and a dessert in Chinatown. Ask about ingredients to suit your preferences.
days.planB: Use indoor exhibitions and cafés around Charoen Krung during a downpour; return to the walking lanes when it clears.

days.title: Design, shopping & a green escape
days.pace: Indoors at midday, outdoors later
days.note: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre normally closes on Mondays. Check the current programme and swap in the Siam shops if needed.

stops.title: Jim Thompson House
stops.detail: Start with the house museum and gardens. Check the visit arrangements before choosing your morning slot.

stops.title: Bangkok Art and Culture Centre
stops.detail: Choose a current exhibition rather than trying to see every floor.

stops.title: Lunch & browsing in Siam
stops.detail: Use the hottest part of the afternoon for food, design shops or an air-conditioned break.

stops.title: Benchakitti Park
stops.detail: Take the train towards Sukhumvit, then slow down with a walk through the park as the heat eases.

stops.title: Dinner near your return route
stops.detail: Choose a neighbourhood restaurant around Sukhumvit or head back towards your hotel.

days.food: A Siam food court gives the group different lunch choices. At dinner, pick a shared Thai meal or a simpler noodle-and-rice option near your hotel.
days.planB: If rain persists, keep the museum, exhibitions and Siam. Move the park to a clearer afternoon.

days.title: Markets & a flexible finish
days.pace: A lighter day with room for departure
days.note: Use the main Chatuchak market on a weekend. On a weekday, give the food market and Ari more time; confirm individual market and shop hours.

stops.title: Chatuchak, if it is the weekend
stops.detail: Browse a few sections with a meeting point agreed in advance. Weekday alternative: start with the food-market stop below.

stops.title: Or Tor Kor food market
stops.detail: Explore produce and prepared food, then choose an easy lunch rather than booking another attraction.

stops.title: Ari cafés & side streets
stops.detail: Take a final neighbourhood wander and a coffee break, keeping luggage and departure logistics in mind.

stops.title: Leave a real departure buffer
stops.detail: Return for bags or take a longer break if you are staying on. Plan the airport journey separately.

days.food: Choose a market lunch and fruit, or a café meal in Ari. The last day is deliberately flexible rather than another reservation-heavy route.
days.planB: Replace outdoor browsing with a café and an indoor shopping stop. Shorten this day first if your flight is early.

bookings.label: Grand Palace admission
bookings.note: Check the official calendar and dress code.

bookings.label: Jim Thompson House
bookings.note: Check current visit and ticket arrangements.

sources.label: Tourism Authority of Thailand · Talat Noi
Tourism Authority of Thailand · Or To Ko

guides.title: Hong Kong in 4 days
guides.subtitle: Harbour lights. Hilltop views. Dim sum between stops.
guides.intro: A first visit that balances the skyline with street-level Hong Kong: Central, Kowloon, an island day and a quieter neighbourhood finish. Let the weather decide when you go up high.
guides.base: Central or Sheung Wan suits Hong Kong Island exploring; Tsim Sha Tsui is convenient for the Kowloon waterfront. Choose proximity to an MTR station over a long daily taxi ride.
guides.transport: Use the MTR for longer hops and ferries when the crossing is part of the day. Leave extra time for Lantau; check the cable car and ferry operators before setting out.
guides.packing: Walking shoes for steep streets, a light layer for air-conditioned interiors, a compact umbrella and sun protection. The Lantau day includes steps and outdoor time.

days.title: Old Town Central & the Peak
days.pace: Street-level exploring, then a view
days.note: Put the Peak on your clearest day. In low cloud, keep exploring Central and move the viewpoint to another afternoon.

stops.title: Sheung Wan & Man Mo Temple
stops.detail: Start with the older streets around Hollywood Road and a respectful visit to the temple.

stops.title: PMQ & the Central lanes
stops.detail: Browse design shops and small streets without turning the morning into a shopping checklist.

stops.title: Dim sum or a café lunch
stops.detail: Take a lunch break around Central or Soho before heading uphill.

stops.title: The Peak
stops.detail: Choose the tram or another transport option, then allow time to enjoy the view instead of immediately returning.

stops.title: Dinner back in Central
stops.detail: Keep the last meal near your return route, with time for a harbourfront stroll if you still have energy.

days.food: Choose dim sum or wonton noodles at lunch. For dinner, Central gives you Cantonese dishes or a wide choice of other cuisines.
days.planB: Stay in Central's galleries, shops and cafés when visibility is poor. Save the Peak for a clearer window.

days.title: Kowloon, from the harbour to the streets
days.area: Star Ferry → Tsim Sha Tsui → Jordan
days.pace: Waterfront first, a lively evening later
days.note: Museum exhibitions and small businesses have separate opening calendars. Check the current programme before committing to an indoor visit.

stops.title: Cross Victoria Harbour
stops.detail: Take the Star Ferry to Tsim Sha Tsui as part of the journey, not just a way to tick off a view.

stops.title: Tsim Sha Tsui promenade
stops.detail: Walk the waterfront and the Avenue of Stars with the skyline across the water.

stops.title: Lunch in Tsim Sha Tsui
stops.detail: Step back from the waterfront for a sit-down meal and a break from walking.

stops.title: Hong Kong Museum of Art or a slow afternoon
stops.detail: Choose an exhibition that interests you, or keep the afternoon for neighbourhood exploring.

stops.title: Temple Street & Jordan
stops.detail: Explore the evening streets, then choose dinner rather than trying to fit every market into one night.

days.food: Try a cha chaan teng lunch or a noodle shop. Around Jordan, compare menus for claypot rice or a shared Cantonese dinner.
days.planB: Use the museum and an indoor meal during rain, then return to the harbour when conditions improve.

days.title: A day on Lantau
days.area: Tung Chung → Ngong Ping → optional Tai O
days.pace: A full island day; keep the evening free
days.note: Ngong Ping 360 has announced a cable-car maintenance closure on 10 November 2026. Check current notices for your dates. Skip Tai O if you prefer a slower return.

stops.title: Travel to Tung Chung
stops.detail: Leave room for the MTR journey and queues before your cable-car reservation.

stops.title: Ngong Ping 360
stops.detail: Ride up towards Ngong Ping if the service is running and conditions are suitable.

stops.title: Big Buddha & Po Lin Monastery
stops.detail: Explore the monastery area and decide whether the steps up to the Buddha suit your group.

stops.title: A relaxed lunch
stops.detail: Eat around Ngong Ping before deciding how much more you want to do.

stops.title: Tai O, or return at your own pace
stops.detail: Optional: continue by local transport to the fishing village. Otherwise head back without adding another leg.

days.food: A vegetarian meal around the monastery is one option. If continuing to Tai O, try a village snack or a sit-down meal before returning.
days.planB: For cable-car closures, assess the official alternative transport and the weather. In severe weather, swap the entire island day for indoor city activities.

days.title: Neighbourhood finds & a harbour farewell
days.pace: Small shops, good food, an open afternoon
days.note: Choose either a museum visit or a longer waterfront break in the afternoon. Shorten this route around your departure.

stops.title: Sham Shui Po's market streets
stops.detail: Explore a few specialist streets and watch the neighbourhood go about its morning.

stops.title: Tai Nan Street cafés & makers
stops.detail: Browse independent shops and pause for a drink rather than rushing between districts.

stops.title: A neighbourhood lunch
stops.detail: Choose a local café or noodle shop before making your way towards West Kowloon.

stops.title: West Kowloon waterfront or M+
stops.detail: Finish outdoors in good weather, or book an exhibition if that is more your pace.

days.food: Try a Hong Kong-style café breakfast, then a noodle lunch or dim sum. Keep the final afternoon flexible for the journey home.
days.planB: Book an indoor museum visit after checking its opening day, or stay with the cafés and shops near your hotel.

bookings.label: The Peak & Peak Tram
bookings.note: Choose a clear-weather window; compare ticket options.

bookings.label: Ngong Ping 360
bookings.note: Check maintenance and weather notices first.

bookings.label: M+ exhibitions
bookings.note: Optional on the final day; check opening times.

sources.label: Hong Kong Tourism Board · Old Town Central
Hong Kong Tourism Board · Sham Shui Po

guides.title: London in 4 days
guides.subtitle: Royal landmarks. Riverside walks. A night at the theatre.
guides.intro: Four days organised by area: Westminster, the City and South Bank, the West End, then Greenwich. Mix a few booked highlights with the freedom to stop at a market or stay longer in a museum.
guides.base: Look near a useful Tube station in Bloomsbury, Covent Garden or Southwark. Compare the actual route to your first stop rather than hotel distance from a single landmark.
guides.transport: Use the Tube between neighbourhood clusters, walk within each area, and consider a river boat for Greenwich. Check TfL for your dates and use the same payment method consistently.
guides.packing: Comfortable walking shoes, a waterproof layer and something warmer for the river. Keep an indoor alternative ready for changeable weather.

days.title: Royal London & the South Bank
days.pace: A classic first day, mostly outdoors
days.note: Buckingham Palace is an exterior stop here. Book separately for any palace interior or Abbey visit, checking the dates and service schedule.

stops.title: Buckingham Palace, from outside
stops.detail: Begin with the palace frontage, then leave time to enjoy the surrounding streets and park.

stops.title: St James's Park
stops.detail: Take the park route towards Westminster rather than adding another transfer.

stops.title: Westminster & Big Ben
stops.detail: See Parliament Square and the river. Choose an Abbey interior visit only if you have allowed for its ticket slot.

stops.title: Lunch & a South Bank stroll
stops.detail: Cross Westminster Bridge, then make the afternoon a relaxed walk with places to sit along the river.

stops.title: Dinner around Waterloo or Covent Garden
stops.detail: Pick the area that suits your hotel and energy rather than another attraction-heavy evening.

days.food: A café breakfast and a South Bank lunch keep the route simple. For dinner, choose a pub meal or one of Covent Garden's many cuisines.
days.planB: Book an indoor Westminster visit or spend longer in an indoor gallery; leave the riverside walk for a clearer spell.

days.title: The Tower, the bridge & Bankside
days.area: Tower Hill → Tower Bridge → Borough → Bankside
days.pace: One major ticket, then a riverside afternoon
days.note: Reserve the Tower of London and leave a substantial morning for it. Tower Bridge's exterior and paid exhibition are different experiences.

stops.title: Tower of London
stops.detail: Give the fortress and Crown Jewels a proper morning; queues can change the pace.

stops.title: Tower Bridge
stops.detail: Walk across for the river views. Add the exhibition only if you want a longer stop.

stops.title: Lunch around Borough Market
stops.detail: Browse before choosing lunch, and check the market calendar for the day of your visit.

stops.title: Bankside & Tate Modern
stops.detail: Keep walking by the river or choose a gallery visit that matches your interests.

days.food: Make Borough your food stop, with something from a market trader or a nearby seated restaurant. Dinner can stay around Bankside or your hotel.
days.planB: Keep the Tower and Tate, connecting by public transport if the long river walk is unappealing in the rain.

days.title: Museum morning, West End evening
days.pace: Culture with a proper break before the show
days.note: The British Museum recommends booking ahead; its general collection is free, while some exhibitions charge. Confirm the actual performance time for your chosen show.

stops.title: British Museum
stops.detail: Choose a few galleries before arriving. Two focused hours are more enjoyable than trying to see everything.

stops.title: Lunch in Covent Garden
stops.detail: Wander through the area, then stop for lunch away from your museum visit.

stops.title: Soho & a free afternoon
stops.detail: Browse, take a café break or head back to rest before the evening.

stops.title: Early dinner, then your West End show
stops.detail: Choose a nearby pre-theatre meal and arrive for the time printed on your ticket.

days.food: Pick a Covent Garden lunch, then choose a pre-theatre menu or an early meal in Soho. Keep time for the walk to the correct theatre.
days.planB: This is already an indoor-friendly day. Replace the shopping wander with an extra gallery or a longer café break.

days.title: A slower day in Greenwich
days.pace: An easy final day, shortened for departure
days.note: The Royal Observatory has announced renovation closure from 2 November 2026; this route uses the park and other museums instead. Check current museum and boat schedules, and shorten the day for departure.

stops.title: Arrive in Greenwich
stops.detail: Use a river boat if the journey appeals, or rail and the DLR if that suits your route better.

stops.title: National Maritime Museum or Queen's House
stops.detail: Choose one indoor visit rather than trying to complete every Greenwich attraction.

stops.title: Greenwich lunch
stops.detail: Browse the market area and choose lunch according to the day's opening stalls.

stops.title: Greenwich Park & the view
stops.detail: Walk uphill only if it suits your group; leave a generous margin for bags and your onward journey.

days.food: Choose a market lunch or a café meal in Greenwich. If you have an early departure, move this whole day earlier in the trip.
days.planB: Choose the museums and a seated lunch. Use rail for the return if weather or schedules make the boat inconvenient.

bookings.label: Tower of London
bookings.note: Reserve a morning and allow for queues.

bookings.label: British Museum entry
bookings.note: Book a free general-entry slot; exhibitions may charge.

bookings.label: West End theatre
bookings.note: Choose a show, date and seats before planning dinner.

sources.label: Historic Royal Palaces · Tower of London

guides.title: Paris in 4 days
guides.subtitle: Big landmarks. Small streets. Time for another coffee.
guides.intro: A first Paris trip with space between the highlights. Give the Louvre its own morning, pair landmarks by neighbourhood, and keep some time for the city beyond its ticket queues.
guides.base: The Marais, Latin Quarter and areas near a useful Métro line make different but practical bases. Compare room size, station access and the actual journey to your booked visits.
guides.transport: Walk within each neighbourhood and use the Métro for bigger jumps. Airport journeys and tickets can differ from ordinary city travel; check the official route before buying.
guides.packing: Comfortable shoes, a compact umbrella and layers. Keep booked entry times available offline and leave room in the day for security queues and café breaks.

days.title: The Eiffel Tower & the Left Bank
days.pace: One booked morning, an optional museum afternoon
days.note: Book the Eiffel Tower if going up matters to you. Orsay closes on Mondays; swap this afternoon with another day when needed.

stops.title: Trocadéro views
stops.detail: Start across the river for a first look at the tower, then walk towards your booked entry.

stops.title: Eiffel Tower or Champ de Mars
stops.detail: Go up with a reservation, or enjoy the tower from ground level and keep the morning flexible.

stops.title: Lunch around Rue Cler
stops.detail: Take a proper lunch and a neighbourhood stroll before deciding on the afternoon.

stops.title: Musée d'Orsay
stops.detail: Choose a focused museum visit, or replace it with a Seine walk if you prefer a lighter day.

days.food: A boulangerie breakfast and a café or market-street lunch fit the route. Choose a bistro dinner near your hotel rather than another long transfer.
days.planB: Keep your booked indoor visits, but move the tower viewpoint or riverside stroll to a clearer spell.

days.title: The Louvre & the grand perspective
days.area: Louvre → Tuileries → Champs-Élysées → Arc de Triomphe
days.pace: Museum first, then an adjustable city walk
days.note: The Louvre closes on Tuesdays. Choose a timed entry and a few priority galleries; use the Métro to shorten the afternoon if needed.

stops.title: A focused Louvre visit
stops.detail: Pick the galleries you most want to see instead of treating the museum as a race.

stops.title: Lunch near Palais Royal
stops.detail: Step away from the museum for a seated lunch before returning to the gardens.

stops.title: Tuileries & Place de la Concorde
stops.detail: Take the garden route west, with time to sit rather than walking straight through.

stops.title: Champs-Élysées & Arc de Triomphe
stops.detail: Walk part of the avenue or use the Métro. The rooftop is a separate ticket choice.

days.food: Choose a casual lunch around Palais Royal or the surrounding streets. Keep dinner simple after a full museum-and-walking day.
days.planB: Use the covered passages and cafés around the Palais Royal and Opéra area instead of the long outdoor axis.

days.title: The islands & the Latin Quarter
days.area: Île de la Cité → Latin Quarter → Saint-Germain
days.pace: Historic sights with a long afternoon break
days.note: Check current entry arrangements for Notre-Dame and reserve Sainte-Chapelle if visiting inside. Leave time for security and worship-related access changes.

stops.title: Notre-Dame & Île de la Cité
stops.detail: Begin around the cathedral and the island. Add an interior visit according to the official visitor arrangements.

stops.title: Sainte-Chapelle
stops.detail: Choose a timed visit for the stained glass, then cross towards the Left Bank.

stops.title: Lunch & the Latin Quarter
stops.detail: Explore a few streets, stop for lunch and resist filling every gap with another monument.

stops.title: Luxembourg Gardens
stops.detail: Take a chair, enjoy the gardens and give your feet a break before dinner.

stops.title: Saint-Germain evening
stops.detail: Finish with a café or bistro meal and a shorter walk through the neighbourhood.

days.food: Choose a crêpe or café lunch in the Latin Quarter, then a bistro dinner in Saint-Germain. Booking is useful if you have a particular restaurant in mind.
days.planB: Use the booked Sainte-Chapelle visit and a longer indoor café stop, shortening the garden walk if the weather turns.

days.title: Montmartre morning, Marais afternoon
days.pace: Two neighbourhoods, with one Métro transfer
days.note: Montmartre involves slopes and steps. Adjust the approach for your group, then leave the afternoon flexible around departure.

stops.title: Sacré-Cœur & Montmartre
stops.detail: Start with the hilltop and quieter streets before settling into the neighbourhood.

stops.title: Abbesses & a late breakfast
stops.detail: Browse small streets and stop at a bakery or café instead of rushing to the next district.

stops.title: Le Marais
stops.detail: Take the Métro across town, then explore the shops, courtyards and streets at your own pace.

stops.title: Place des Vosges or Musée Carnavalet
stops.detail: Choose an outdoor pause or an indoor history visit after checking the museum calendar.

days.food: Start with a Montmartre bakery or café, then choose falafel, a sandwich or a seated lunch in the Marais. Leave a final coffee stop if time permits.
days.planB: Choose the museum and covered shopping streets after checking opening days. Move this day earlier if departure is in the morning.

bookings.label: Eiffel Tower
bookings.note: Choose stairs or lift and the level you want.

bookings.label: Louvre timed entry
bookings.note: Closed Tuesdays; select the right visitor category.

bookings.label: Sainte-Chapelle
bookings.note: Book a slot and allow for security.

sources.label: Paris je t'aime · Louvre to Arc route

guides.title: Istanbul in 4 days
guides.subtitle: Two continents. Ferry rides. Layers of history.
guides.intro: Start with the historic peninsula, then give the bazaars, Beyoğlu and the Asian side their own days. A few ferry crossings and long meal breaks make the city easier to enjoy.
guides.currencyNote: Budget shown in EUR as a planning reference; local prices and payments are generally in Turkish lira (TRY). Check exchange rates and current admission prices before booking.
guides.base: Sultanahmet suits an early start at the historic sights. Karaköy or Galata suits café and ferry access, but check slopes and the walk with luggage before choosing a hotel.
guides.transport: Combine walking, trams and scheduled ferries. Check the operator's actual route and departure time; a useful cross-city ferry can also provide some of the trip's best views.
guides.packing: Walking shoes with grip for slopes and cobbles, layers for ferry decks, and modest clothing for mosque visits. Follow each religious site's visitor instructions.

days.title: The historic peninsula
days.pace: A compact route with time for the major sights
days.note: Mosque access changes around prayers. Hagia Sophia's visitor route and admission arrangements differ from worship access; verify current instructions before visiting.

stops.title: Sultanahmet Square & the Hippodrome
stops.detail: Begin outdoors to understand the area before stepping into its busiest sights.

stops.title: Blue Mosque
stops.detail: Visit respectfully outside prayer closures, following the current dress and access rules.

stops.title: Hagia Sophia
stops.detail: Choose the official visitor experience or enjoy the exterior if a lighter day suits your group.

stops.title: A Sultanahmet lunch break
stops.detail: Pause for a meal and rest before another indoor visit.

stops.title: Basilica Cistern
stops.detail: Allow time for the underground space and its atmosphere, checking the operator's current tickets.

days.food: Try a simple köfte or vegetable-based lunch, then choose a relaxed dinner near your hotel. There is no need to add a cross-city food trip on this first day.
days.planB: Keep the cistern and a longer indoor lunch during rain. Move mosque visits around the actual prayer and visitor schedules.

days.title: Palace courtyards & the bazaars
days.pace: A long palace morning, an adjustable afternoon
days.note: Topkapı closes on Tuesdays. Bazaar trading days can vary; keep market stops flexible and check holiday arrangements before setting out.

stops.title: Topkapı Palace
stops.detail: Choose the ticket that covers the sections you want, then allow a generous morning for the palace.

stops.title: Gülhane & a lunch break
stops.detail: Slow down after the palace with some greenery and a meal nearby.

stops.title: Grand Bazaar
stops.detail: Browse a few lanes with a meeting point agreed in advance. Shopping is optional, not another task to complete.

stops.title: Spice Bazaar & Eminönü
stops.detail: Continue towards the waterfront, with a short tram ride or a walk depending on your energy.

days.food: A lokanta lunch is an easy way to compare dishes. Finish with tea and something sweet near Eminönü, or choose a waterfront meal after checking the menu.
days.planB: Give the palace and covered market areas more time, leaving the park and waterfront for a clearer day.

days.title: Galata, Karaköy & Beyoğlu
days.pace: A neighbourhood day with an optional art stop
days.note: This route includes hills. Use public transport for an uphill stretch and check museum opening days if choosing the indoor visit.

stops.title: Galata streets & the tower exterior
stops.detail: Explore around the tower before the busiest part of the day. Going inside is an optional paid addition.

stops.title: Karaköy cafés & lunch
stops.detail: Walk down towards the water and take a long lunch break in the neighbourhood.

stops.title: Istanbul Modern or the waterfront
stops.detail: Choose a current exhibition or keep the afternoon outdoors, rather than automatically doing both.

stops.title: Beyoğlu & İstiklal Avenue
stops.detail: Return uphill using transport if useful, then explore the avenue and its side streets before dinner.

days.food: Choose a Karaköy café meal or a simple local lunch, then compare meyhane-style shared plates and other dinner options around Beyoğlu.
days.planB: Choose Istanbul Modern and indoor café stops, replacing the longer outdoor wander if it is wet or windy.

days.title: Across to Kadıköy & Moda
days.pace: Food, neighbourhood streets and a seaside pause
days.note: Check Şehir Hatları's current sailing times and allow a large return buffer if departing today. Ferry services can change with weather.

stops.title: A scheduled ferry to Kadıköy
stops.detail: Choose a departure pier that suits your hotel and let the crossing be part of the morning.

stops.title: Kadıköy market streets
stops.detail: Browse food shops and local streets before settling on lunch.

stops.title: A long Kadıköy lunch
stops.detail: Choose a lokanta meal, a café lunch or shared dishes according to the group's preferences.

stops.title: Moda waterfront & a final tea
stops.detail: Finish with a seaside walk, then return with plenty of time for luggage and onward travel.

days.food: This is the day to leave room for snacks: a market lunch, tea and a pastry or dessert in Moda. Pick what suits your diet rather than ordering every local speciality.
days.planB: If ferry conditions are poor, swap with the palace or museum day. For an early flight, move Kadıköy earlier rather than rushing the return.

bookings.label: Topkapı Palace
bookings.note: Closed Tuesdays; compare the official ticket inclusions.

bookings.label: Basilica Cistern
bookings.note: Check the operator's current tickets and visitor hours.

bookings.label: Istanbul Modern
bookings.note: Optional; check exhibition dates and opening days.

bookings.label: Şehir Hatları ferries
bookings.note: Use current timetables for your actual travel date.
